title: Accuracy Is Not Always We Need: Precision-Aware Bayesian Yield Optimization
problem: Integrated circuit yield optimization requires intensive simulation but existing methods uniformly allocate computational resources across all design candidates regardless of their quality potential, resulting in wasteful evaluation and slow convergence.
motivation: Resource-efficient yield estimation is critical for reducing time-to-market in semiconductor manufacturing, where simulation cost is a major bottleneck.
method: The approach uses a statistical model to learn how well different simulation quality levels predict actual chip yield, so it can tell when a fast, rough simulation is reliable enough. It then continuously adjusts the simulation quality for each design based on what it learns about that design's promise — running more precise simulations on promising candidates and rougher ones on less likely designs. This smart allocation of simulation detail converges using fewer than 1,000 total simulations, over 10 times fewer than traditional methods.
key_novelty: The key insight is using variable simulation quality (continuous precision levels rather than fixed predefined counts) that adapts to each design's predicted quality, so better designs get more expensive detailed simulations and weaker ones get cheaper rough ones.
contributions: Precision-aware yield optimization framework with adaptive resource allocation
Continuous AutoRegression model characterizing yield-fidelity relationship
Multi-fidelity acquisition strategy optimizing simulation budget allocation
10x reduction in simulation costs achieving better final designs and robustness
primary_theme: Adaptive multi-fidelity simulation for efficient IC yield optimization
